_meta.why: 2009scape authors a familiar conversation for spirit graahk only and marks its fallback line as likely inauthentic; the porting policy permits a cited external reference when the local method is absent.
_meta.chat_level_rule: Summoning level + 10, agreed by three independent sources: SpiritGraahkDialogue.kt gates a level-57 familiar at 67, FamiliarDialoguePlugin's commented-out pet gate reads getSummoningLevel() + 10, and Transcript:Spirit wolf splits a level-1 familiar at 11.
_meta.below_gate_rule: Below the gate the familiar makes its noise without the translation. Transcript:Spirit wolf is the only page that records the split and that is what it shows: 'Whurf?' below level 11, 'Whurf? (What are you doing?)' at 11+.
_meta.held_out: Conditional conversations keep their condition text but stay out of the random pool; overhead lines are ambient chat, not Interact.

lines.text: Whurf? (What are you doing?)
Oh, just some...biped things. I'm sure it would bore you.
Bark! Bark! (Danger!)
Where?!
Whiiiine... (False alarm...)
Whuff whuff. Pantpant awf! (I smell something good. Hunting time!)
We can go hunting in a moment. I just have to take care of something first.
Pant pant whine? (When am I going to get to chase something?)
Oh I'm sure we'll find something for you in a bit.
Whuff-whuff! Arf! (Throw the bone! I want to chase!)
I can't just throw bones away - I need them to train my Prayer!

conditional.condition: If the player has any type of bone in their inventory

lines.text: Cluck cluck cluck! (Attack! Fight! Annihilate!)
It always worries me when you're so happy saying that.
Bwaaak... (Can it be fightin' time, please?)
Look I'll find something for you to fight, just give me a second.
Bwuckbwuck bwaak. (I want to fight something.)
I'll find something for you in a minute - just be patient.
Screeeee. Screescree screeee screee. (This is a fun little walk.)
Why do I get the feeling you'll change your tune when I start loading you up with items?

conversations.condition: With Spirit terrorbird having 10 or less items in inventory

lines.text: Screeeeeeee screeee screeeeeeee. (I can keep this up for hours.)
I'm glad, as we still have plenty of time to go.

conversations.condition: With Spirit terrorbird having 11 items in inventory

lines.text: Scree scree screeeeeeee? (Are we going to visit a bank soon?)
I'm not sure, you still have plenty of room for more stuff.
Screescreeee screeescreeeeee screeee? (Just don't leave it too long, okay?)

conversations.condition: With Spirit terrorbird having 12 items in inventory

lines.text: Clickerclick? (Where are we going?)
I've not decided yet.
Clatterclick... (Fine, don't tell me...)
Oh, okay, well, we are going...
Clacker! (Don't want to know now.)
Siiiigh...spiders.
Clackclackclatter? (Who is that?)
Who?
Clatterclatterclickclacker. (The two-legs over there.)
I can't see who you mean...
Clickclatter... (Never mind...)
Can you describe them a little better...
Clack! (It doesn't matter now.)
Siiiigh...spiders.
Clickerclack? (What are you doing?)
Nothing that you should concern yourself with.
Clatterclickclack... (I see, you don't think I‘m smart enough to understand...)
That's not it at all! Look, I was...
Clack! (Don't wanna know now.)
Siiiigh...spiders.
Click... (Sigh...)
What is it now?
Clatter. (Nothing really.)
Oh, well that's a relief.
Clatterclatter? (So. do I get any of those flies?)
I don't know, I was saving these for a pet.
Clatter... (I see...)
Look, you can have some if you want.
Clatterclackclatterclatter! (Oh, don't do me any favours.)
Look, here, have some!
Clack! (Don't want them now.)
Siiiigh...spiders.

conditional.condition: If the player has flies in inventory

lines.text: Slitherslime slitherslither schlorp schlorp. (All this running around the place is fun!)
I'll bet it's a step up from your usually sedentary lifestyle!
Schlorpschlorp slither slime. (True, but it's mostly seeing the sort of sights you don't get at home.)
Such as?
Schlorpschlorp slither. (Living things for a start.)
Those are in short supply in Mort Myre, I admit.
Schurpschlurp shclurp... (I think my stomach is drying out...)
Your stomach? How do you know how it's feeling?
SIitherslither slitherslither... (I am walking on it, you know...)
Urrgh...
Schlurpschlurp schlurpslitherslime schlurp? (Okay, Ihave to ask, what are those things you people totter about on?)
You mean my legs?
Schlurp. Schlurpslither slitherslither schlurp? (Yes, those. How are you supposed to eat anything through them?)
Well, we don't. That's what our mouths are for.
Schlurp! Slither slither slitherslither slime schlurp. (Oh, right! Ithought those were for expelling waste gas and hot air!)
Well, for a lot of people they are.
Schlorpschlorp. (Can you slow down?)
Are we going too fast for you?
Slitherslimeslither schlorp slitherslither slithersclorp! (I bet if you had to run on your internal organs you'd want a break every now and then!)
Schlorp... (...)
What's the matter?
Schlorpslither sclorp... (Check your head...)
What about it... Oh, wait! Oh, this is pretty awkward...
Slitherslimeslither slime slime slither schlorp... (You're wearing the spine of one of my relatives as a hat.)
Well more of a faux-pas, then.
Schlorp schlorp slither... (Just a bit...)

conditional.condition: If the player is wearing a snelm

lines.text: Clickclickchiner! (Rock fish now, please?)
Not right now. I don't have any rock fish.
Clickclickchitter? (When can we go fishing? I want rock fish.)
When I need some fish. It's not that hard to work out, right?
Clickclickchitter! (I'm stealthy!)
Errr... of course you are.
Chitterclick? (Can I have some fish?)
No, I have to cook these for later.
Clickclickclick? (Free fish, please?)
No...I already told you you can't.
Clickclickclick... (Can it be fish time soon?)
Great...I get stuck with the only granite crab in existence that can't take no for an answer...

conditional.condition: If the player has 7 or more fish in inventory

lines.text: Whiiine whiiiiine? (You have lovely ankles.)
Am I meant to be pleased by that?
Whiiliiinewhiiiiiiine whiiiiiiiine. (Thin skin. Your delicious blood is easier to get to.)
I knew I couldn't trust you.
Whiiiiiiiiiiiiine! (Oh, come on, you won't feel a thing...)
Whiiiiiine! (How about that local sports team?)
Which one? The gnomeball team?
Whiiiiine whiiiiine whinewhiiiine. (I must confess: I have no idea.)
Why did you ask, then?
Whiiliiine whiiiiinewhiiine. (I was just trying to be friendly.)
Just trying to get to my veins, more like!
Whiiliine whinewhiiiine? (Have you ever tasted pirate blood?)
Why would I drink pirate blood?
Whiiliine whiiiiiiiiiiiiine? (How about dwarf blood?)
I don't think you quite understand...
Whine? (Gnome blood, then?)
Whiiliiine! (I'm soooo hungry!)
What would you like to eat?
Whiiiine, whiiiinewhiiiiine whine... (Well, if you're not too attached to your elbow...)
You can't eat my elbow! You don't have teeth!
Whiiliiine whinewhiiiiiiine! (Tell me about it. Cousin Nigel always makes fun of me. Calls me 'No-teeth'.)
Hssshsss ssss ssssss...Hssshsssssss sssssss sshss. (This is so unsafe... I should have a hard-hat for this work.)
Well, I could get you a rune helm if you like - those are pretty hard.
Hssss ssssshssshssss ssss. (Keep that up and you'll have the union on your back, lad/lass.)
Hsshssshssssss ssssss! (You can't touch me, I'm part ofthe union!)
Is that some official 'no-touching' policy or something?
Sssssshsssss sssss hsssss...(You really don't get it, do you Player?)
Hsss sssss hssssss sssshssshsssss. (You know, you might want to register with the union.)
What are the benefits?
Hssshssshsss sss sssss ssshsss. (I stop bugging you to join the union.)
Ask that again later; I'll have to consider that generous proposal.
Hssshsss sss hsssshsss ssss? (Why are you ignoring that good ore seam, lad/lass?)
Which ore seam?
Hssshssshss sss ssssss ssssshssss. (There's a good seam of ore right underneath us at the moment.)
Great! How long will it take for you to get to it?
Hssshssss hsss. (Five years, give or take.)
Five years!
THssshsssss hssss ssss hsss. Hssshssssss sssshsss. (That's if we go opencast, mind. I could probably reach it in three if I just dug.)
Right. I see. I think I'll skip it thanks.
Sssshsss hsss ssshsss? (If you have that pick, why make me dig?)
Because it's a little quicker and easier on my arms.
Sssshsssssshsss ssssss hssss... (I should take industrial action over this...)
You mean you won't work for me any more?
Hsssss. Ssssshsssshsssss sss ssssshssss. (No. It means me and the lads feed you legs-first into some industrial machinery, maybe the Blast Furnace.)
I'll just be over here, digging.
Ssssshssssss! (That's the spirit, lad/lass!)

conditional.condition: when wielding pickaxe

lines.text: Clickclickclack click click click? (Hey, boss, how about we go to the bank?)
And do what?
Screescree scree, 'Click!' (Well, we could open by shouting, 'Stand and deliver!'
Why does everything with you end with something getting held up?
Clickclick! Clickclick click scree. (That isn't true! Give me One example.)
How about the post office?
Screescree? (How about another?)
Those junior White Knights? The ones selling the gnome crunchies?
Screeclick click. (That was self defence.)
No! No more hold-ups, stick-ups, thefts, or heists, you got that?
Screeclickclick clicklick! (Say hello to my little friend!)
What?
Clickclicklick screescree. (My little friend: you ignored him last time you met him.)
So, who is your friend?
Clickclick click clik screee? (If I tell you, what is the point?)
Clickclick click scree click. (Hey, boss, I've been thinking.)
That's never a good sign.
Screeclick click screee... (See, I heard about this railway...)
We are not robbing it!
Screeclickclick click scree click... (I might not have wanted to suggest that, boss...)
Then what were you going to suggest?
Clickclick click click click. (That isn't important right now.)
I thought as much.
Scree clickclick click click? (Why do we never go to crossroads and rob travellers?)
There are already highwaymen at the good spots.
Clickclick scree click. (Maybe we need to think bigger.)
How's it going, Tz-Kih?
Pree pree? (Pray pray?)
Don't start with all that again.
Squee, squee squee. (Hmph, silly JalYt.)
Squee squeepree pree squee? (Does JalYt think Tz-Kih as strong as Jad Jad?)
Are you as strong as TzTok-Jad? Yeah, sure, why not.
Sqee? Sqee sqee. Sqee sqee. (Really? Thanks, JalYt. Tz-Kih strong and happy.)
Squee squeepree pree squee? (Have you heard of blood bat JalYt?)
Blood bats? You mean vampyre bats?
Sqee. Sqee sqee. (Yes. Blood bat.)
Yes, I've heard of them. What about them?
Squee squee squeesquee, squee pree pree. Squee squee. (Tz-Kih like blood bat, but drink pray pray not blood blood. Blood blood is yuck.)
Thanks, Tz-Kih, that's nice to know.
Pree pree, preepree pree pree preepree! (Pray pray, pray pray pray pray pray pray!)
Calm down, Tz-Kih, we'll find you something to drink soon.
Pree preeeeeeeeeeeeee! (Pray praaaaaaaaaaaaaay!)
Okay, okay. Calm down!
Squee squee pree, squee squee pree. (You drink pray, me drink pray.)
What's that, Tz-Kih?
Squeepree. Squee squee pree. (You got pray pray pot Tz-Kih drink pray pray you, you drink pray pray pot.)
You want to drink my Prayer points?
Squee. Pree pree. (Yes. Pray pray.)
Err, not right now, Tz-Kih. I, er, need them myself.
Sorry.
Squee, pree preeee...? (But, pray praaaay...?)

conditional.condition: With at least one dose of prayer potion in the inventory

lines.text: Squeak squeak squeesqueak! (Hey boss, we going to do anything wicked today?)
Well, I don't know why we would: I tend not to go around being wicked.
Squeesquee? (Not even a little?)
Well there was that one time...
I'm sorry, no wickedness today.
Squeeeeee... (Awwwwww...)
Squee squee squee squeak squeak? (Hey boss, can we go and loot something now?)
Well, what did you have in mind?
Squeaksqueak? (I dunno - where are we headed?)
I hadn't decided yet.
Squeak squeak squeak squeeee! (When we get there, let's loot something nearby!)
Sounds like a plan, certainly.
Squeak squeeesquee squeak? (So what we up to today, boss?)
Oh I'm sure we'll find something to occupy our time.
Squeaksqueak squee sqeee! (Let's go robbin' graves again!)
What do you mean 'again'?
Squee... (Nuffin'...)
Squeesqueak squeak squeaksqueak. (You know, boss, I don't think you're totally into this whole 'evil' thing.)
I wonder what gave you that impression?
Squreaksqueak squeak squee squeaksquee. (Well, I worked with a lot of evil people; some of the best)
Such as?
Squeaksquak! Squeesquee squeaksquee. (I'm not telling! I've got my principles to uphold.)
There is honour amongst thieves, it would seem.
Clatter clatteryclatter hss. (This activity is not optimal for us.)
Well, you'll just have to put up with it for now.
Click click hsshsshsss hsssss. (We would not have to 'put up' with this in the hive.)
Clack hiss hiss clatter. Clack clatter? (We are growing infuriated. What is our goal?)
Well, I haven't quite decided yet.
Clack clack clack hsss. (There is no indecision in the hive.)
Or a sense of humour or patience, it seems.
Hssshssshsss hss click clatter clack. (We find this to be wasteful of our time.)
Maybe I find you wasteful...
Clackclack clackclackclack hsss... (We would not face this form of abuse in the hive.)
Click clatter clatter hssshsshsss. (We grow tired of your antics, biped.)
What antics? I'm just getting on with my day.
Hsshsshss clatter. Click click click hsshsssclatter. (In an inefficient way. In the hive, you would be replaced.)
In the hive this, in the hive that...
Hsssssssssssssssss! (How dare you!)
How dare I what?
Hsssclick click clatter! (That weapon offends us!)
What weapon?
Oh...
Awkward.

lines.text: Schlorp sclorp sclorp! (Oi've gotta braand new comboine 'aarvester!)
A what?
Schlorp schlurp sclorpsclorp splutter. (Well, it's a flat bit a metal wi' a 'andle that i can use ta 'aarvest all combinations o' plaants.)
You mean a spade?
Schlurpschlorp. (Aye, 'aat'll be it.)
Schlorp, splort, splort, splutter shclorp? (What we be doin' 'ere, zur?)
Oh, I have a few things to take care of here, is all.
Schorp, splutter, splutter. Schlup schorp. (Aye, right ye are, zur. Oi'll be roight there.)
Schlurp...schlorpschlorp schlurp splutter? (Errr...are ye gonna eat that?)
Eat what?
Schlurpschlurp, schlorp schlorp. (Y've got summat on yer, goin' wastin'.)
Ewwww!
Schlurp splutter? (So ye don' want it then?)
No I do not want it! Nor do I want to put my boot in your mouth for you to clean it off.
Splutter? (An' why not?)
It'll likely come out dirtier than when I put it in!
Splutter schlorp schlorp... (Oi wus just a-wonderin'...)
Oh! What have you been eating! Your breath is making my eyes water!
Splutter! Splooge. (Oi! Oi'm 'urt by thaat.)
Sorry.
Splutter splorch schlorp sclorp. (Oi mean, oi even et some mints earlier.)
You did?
Schlorp schlorp schlup schlorp schlorp splutter shclorp. ('At's roight. Oi found some mint plaants in a big pile o' muck, and oi 'ad 'em fer me breakfast.)
The mystery resolves itself.
Schlorp... (Sigh...)
What's the matter?
Schlupschlup schlopr... (Oi'm not 'appy carryin' round these young'uns where we're going.)
Young'uns? Oh, the buckets of compost!
Well, those wooden containers will keep them safe.
Schlurp, splutter, schlurp. ('Aah, that be a mighty good point, zur.)

conditional.condition: When the compost mound is carrying a bucket of compost or supercompost

lines.text: Wagooly wanay wahoo! (Half a pound of tuppenny rice, half a pound of treacle...)
I hate it when you sing that song.
Wannobly wanay wahoo! (...that's the way the money goes...)
Couldn't you sing 'Kumbaya' or something?
Wooble! Wibbly nooble! (...BANG, goes the chinchompa!)
Sheesh.
Gobbobbly nobble? (What's small, brown and blows up?)
A brown balloon?
Wernibbly doodle! Nooble, nooble. (A chinchompa! Pull my finger.)
I'm not pulling your finger.
Bidoodly dooble. Boooooooble. (Nothing will happen. Truuuuust meeeeee.)
Oh, go away.
Bajooble dagoodle, hooby snooby 'Boo'. (l spy, with my little eye, something beginning with '8'.)
Bomb? Bang? Boom? Blowing-up-little-chipmunk?
Grooby bandoodle. Nobbly bobble. (No. Body odour. You should wash a bit more.)
Well, that was pleasant. You don't smell all that great either, you know.
Wobernuggle, wobernuggle! Bajoobly! (Stop talking, stop talking! Your breath stinks!)
We're never going to get on, are we?
Wanibble boobbly nooble. (I seem to have found a paper bag.)
Well done. Anything in it?
Wanooble de nobble babooble...goombly! (Hmmm. Let me see. It seems to be full of some highly sought after, very expensive...chinchompa breath!)
No, don't pop it!
You just cannot help yourself, can you?
Doogle - de nooble. (Woah, woah, woah - hold up there.)
What is it, ratty?
Gweebel bobbly dooble? (You got something in your backpack that you'd like to tell me about?)
I was wondering when you were going to bring up the chinchompa. I'm sure they like it in my inventory.
Roooowl? Grooooooowl raaaaaw. (Did they not teach you anything in school? Chinchompas die in hot bags.)
Roooowley. Grooooooowl de boogle? (You know what happens when chinchompas die. Are you attached to your back?)
Medically, yes. And I kind of like it too. I get the point.

Just as soon as I find something to attack.

lines.text: Hey mate, how are you?
Not so bad.
Did you know that during the average human life-span the heart will beat approximately 2.5 billion times?
Wow, that is a lot of non-stop work!
Did you know that in one feeding a mosquito can absorb one-and-a-half times its own body weight in blood?
Eugh.
Did you know that Gielinor gets 100 tons heavier every day, due to dust falling from space?
What a fascinating fact.
Did you know that a snail can sleep for three years?
I wish I could do that. Ah...sleep.
Over the course of their lifetime a shark may grow and use 20,000 teeth!
Wow! That is a whole load of teeth. I wonder what the Tooth Fairy would give for those?
Unlike most animals, both the shark's upper and lower jaws move when they bite.
Really?
Yup. Chomp chomp.
Did you know that sharks have the most powerful jaws of any animal on the planet?
No, I didn't.
Full of facts, me.
Did you know that sharks normally eat alone?
I see.
Sometimes one feeding shark attracts others and they all try and get a piece of the prey.
They take a bite at anything in their way and may even bite each other!
Ouch!
Raaar! Mewble, whurf whurf.
Scruunt, scraaan.
Titan?
Yes, boss?
What's that in your hand?
I'm glad you asked that, boss.
This is the first prototype for the Iron Titan (tm) action figure. You just pull this string here and he fights crime with real action sounds.
Titan?
Yes, boss?
Never mind.
Boss!
What?
I've just had a vision of the future.
I didn't know you were a fortune teller. Let's hear it then.
Just imagine, boss, an Iron Titan (tm) on every desk.
That doesn't even make sense.
Hmm. It was a bit blurry, perhaps the future is having technical issues at the moment.
Riiight.
Boss?
Yes, titan?
You know how you're the boss and I'm the titan?
Yes?
Do you think we could swap for a bit?
No, titan!
Aww...
How are you today, titan?
I'm very happy.
That's marvellous, why are you so happy?
Because I love the great taste of Iron Titan cereal (tm)!
You're supposed to be working for me, not promoting yourself.
Sorry, boss.

Barooo, barrrooooooooo... (I was born on a miserable night in Bennath. My mother, bless her soul, died in labour and was eaten by the Fremennik who tended our herd. My father was never about, as he spent much of his time showing the adult females how much he could carry, for how long, and how quickly he could traverse a mountain pass. He was a foolish yak and was laughed at by the herd, though he had no inkling of that. With no obvious father to raise me, I was left very much to my own devices and relied on the generosity of others to make my way through infancy and childhood. I was forced to be cunning, wise and, sometimes, ruthless.)
Baroooooo. (I don't know what it is to be ruth, though. It is a silly word)

Barroobaroooo baaaaaaaaarooo... (When I came of age, the herd pushed me out. It was always this way for an adult whose father still lived. I would have to wander across the Fremennik lands until I found a new herd to join, and I had to hope that the men whose paths I crossed wouldn't decide that I might make a delicious meal. The trolls, too, were a concern, though they were easily avoided and yak-skin is thick and tough. So I set out on my journey, only 8 years old for a human, but already a man in yak society.)
Barrrrooooo. (I'd forgotten how depressing my life is...)

Baroo barrrooooo barooobaaaarrroooo... (When I was an adoscelent, wandering the fields and slopes of my homeland, I knew that I was destined for greatness. Though I was merely a yak, and though all yaks dream of far-off lands and grand adventures, I knew my horns to be sharper than most and my tongue more agile; I was better able to cast my lowing voice across the chasms that separated me from the other yaks, and my voice became a song to the yaks that remained in herds. I, unlike all the others of my kind, was not interested in rejoining society - in my exile I had come to love solitude and the calm sounds between the spaces of silence that the mountains whispered.)

Baaaaaarrrrrrrrooooooooooooo! (Now, I am an adult, with adult cares and adult tastes. My youth is far behind me, as is my natural body. I have ascended from the dull life of the ordinary yak, and now I have come to know and to love all of them. I am the new spirit-ancestor of my people, and they send their dearest thoughts and wishes to me. Ah, but alas: you, my master, have shaken from my eternal reveries and called me here. It is my lot for eternity to have one shard of myself taken now and then, rent from my whole consciousness to rejoin it later, filled with experiences both grand and dull. This is my new tragedy and my new love.)
What a fantastic tale! You've had an amazing life!
Barrooo? Barrrrroooobarooo... (You think so? You should try living it...)
Forward, master/mistress, to a battle that will waken the gods!
I'd rather not, if it's all the same to you.
I shall never meet my end at this rate...
How do you wish to meet your end, master/mistress?
Hopefully not for a very long time.
You do not wish to be torn asunder by the thousand limbs of a horde of demons?
No! I'm quite happy picking flax and turning unstrung bows into gold...
Why must we dawdle when glory awaits?
I'm beginning to think you just want me to die horribly...
We could have deaths that bards sing of for a thousand years.
That's not much compensation.
Master/Mistress, we should be marching into glorious battle!
You know, I think you're onto something.
We could find a death befitting such heroes of Gielinor!
Ah. You know, I'd prefer not to die...
Beneath the claws of a mighty foe shall I be sent into the embrace of death!
Let us go forth to battle, my lord/lady!
Why do you like fighting so much? It's not very nice to kill things.
It is the most honourable thing in life.
But I summoned you, I'm not sure I can even say that you're alive...
Alas, you have discovered the woe of all summoned creatures' existence.
Really? I was right?
Oh, woe...woe!
